roles.title: Software Engineer

responsibilities: Write and review code with a focus on quality, performance, and maintainability.

Promote knowledge sharing by hosting technical deep-dives, contributing to documentation, and enabling cross-team learning.

frameworks.title: Career Tracks & Band Progression
frameworks.summary: Defines two parallel career tracks — an IC Track (ASE → SE → SSE → Lead Eng → Principal Eng → Tech Architect → Principal Architect) and a People Leadership Track (Tech Lead → Sr Tech Lead → Eng Manager → Sr Eng Manager → Director → VP Eng → CTO) — organized into four bands (Contributor, Owner, Leader, Strategic Leader), each with its own scope of influence, complexity, and independence level. Movement between tracks is allowed based on readiness and aspiration.

frameworks.title: Behavioural Competencies (Taazaa Core Values)
frameworks.summary: Six core values — Humility, Craftsmanship, Curiosity, Future Focus, Empathy, and Owns It — define cultural fit, with a progression matrix showing how values such as Empathy, Ownership, Craftsmanship, Future Focus, Collaboration and Communication are expected to manifest differently at each band, from Contributor (e.g. 'Owns tasks,' 'Follows standards') up to Strategic Leader (e.g. 'Owns long-term org success,' 'Shapes future excellence').

frameworks.title: Functional Competency Clusters
frameworks.summary: Seven functional competency clusters — Technical Depth & Craft, System Design & Architecture, Delivery & Execution Discipline, Collaboration & Influence, Problem Solving & System Thinking, Operational Excellence, and Professional Maturity & Communication — with a maturity table showing how Technical Depth, System Design, Execution, Problem Solving, and Ops Excellence each progress from Contributor through Strategic Leader.

frameworks.title: Role Structure & KPIs
frameworks.summary: For every role from ASE up through CTO, defines a Mission statement, an 'Indicator of Excellence' describing what great performance looks like, and paired Lead (predictive) and Lag (outcome) indicators used to measure performance in that role.

frameworks.title: Skills Taxonomy
frameworks.summary: Organizes technical skills into seven skill families — Backend Engineering, Frontend Engineering, Mobile Engineering, Cloud & DevOps, QA & Automation, Architecture & Design, and Data Engineering — each rated across three proficiency levels: Foundation, Practitioner, and Expert.

frameworks.title: RACI Matrix
frameworks.summary: Assigns Responsible/Accountable/Consulted/Informed designations across six role groups (ASE-SE, SSE, TL-STL, Architect, EM, Director+) for six key deliverables: Code Quality, System Design, Architecture Governance, Delivery Predictability, Incident RCA, and Tech Strategy.

frameworks.title: COL Framework (Contributor → Owner → Leader → Strategic Leader)
frameworks.summary: Consolidates the organizational structure for Taazaa's QA & SDET functions using the Contributor → Owner → Leader → Strategic Leader (COL) career-band framework, mapping every role to a band and defining competencies, KPIs, OKRs, and 30-60-90 day milestones for each position. Ensures consistent leveling across the QA (manual/functional) and SDET (automation/tooling) tracks, aligning Behavioural Competencies (Taazaa Core Values) with Functional Competencies to drive cultural fit and delivery excellence.

frameworks.title: QA Track vs. SDET Track
frameworks.summary: Two parallel, equally-prestigious career tracks with movement encouraged between them based on skill readiness and aspiration. QA Track: Associate QA → QA Engineer (Contributor), Senior QA Eng → Lead QA Eng (Owner), Principal QA Engineer (Leader), QA Director+ (Strategic Leader). SDET Track: Associate SDET → SDET I (Contributor), Senior SDET (Owner), Principal SDET (Leader), QA Director+ (Strategic Leader).

frameworks.title: COL Role Bands & Scope of Influence
frameworks.summary: Defines scope of influence, complexity, and independence per band: Contributor (module-level tasks, defined scope, low-medium complexity, needs guidance → partial autonomy), Owner (multi-module/squad-level, medium-high complexity, high autonomy), Leader (product/platform, cross-team, high complexity, high autonomy plus cross-team influence), Strategic Leader (org-wide systems & strategy, very high complexity, drives org direction).

frameworks.title: Behavioural Competencies (Taazaa Core Values)
frameworks.summary: Six core values apply across all QA/SDET bands, each with a progression of expected behavior from Contributor to Strategic Leader: Humility (listens/incorporates feedback → shapes org culture of learning), Craftsmanship (follows QA standards → shapes future QA excellence), Curiosity (learns tools/techniques → defines 2-3 year QA direction), Future Focus (identifies improvements → defines long-term QA strategy), Empathy (understands team constraints → balances org priorities empathetically), Ownership (owns assigned test modules → owns org-wide quality success).

frameworks.title: Functional Competency Clusters
frameworks.summary: Seven functional competency clusters used to describe QA/SDET skill progression by level (Contributor/Owner/Leader/Strategic Leader): (1) Manual Testing & Test Design, (2) Test Automation Development, (3) CI/CD & Pipeline Integration, (4) Performance & Security Testing, (5) Defect Management & Prevention, (6) Collaboration & Influence, (7) Process & Operational Excellence.

frameworks.title: QA and SDET Accountability Matrices
frameworks.summary: Two standard outcome-area/metric/key-activity tables used across the QA track (Defect Detection, Test Coverage, Release Quality, Execution Timeliness, Collaboration, Process Adherence) and SDET track (Automation Coverage, Framework Stability, Pipeline Efficiency, Defect Prevention, Knowledge Sharing), each pairing a measurable outcome with the key activity that drives it.

frameworks.title: RACI Matrix
frameworks.summary: Defines Responsible/Accountable/Consulted/Informed roles across career bands (Assoc QA/SDET, QA Eng/SDET I, Sr QA/Sr SDET, Lead/Principal, QA Director+) for seven deliverables: Test Case Execution, Defect Management, Automation Framework, Test Strategy & Planning, CI/CD QA Integration, QA Governance & Standards, Delivery Predictability, and Release Quality Sign-off.

frameworks.title: 30-60-90 Day Success Milestones
frameworks.summary: Standard onboarding milestone framework for both tracks. QA Eng: 30 days onboard to product/domain/QA processes; 60 days shift-left testing impact visible with 80% functional test coverage; 90 days consistent high-quality releases with minimal production defects. SDET: 30 days onboard to product architecture/codebase/automation framework; 60 days automated tests running reliably in CI/CD with reduced manual regression scope; 90 days automation suite stability >95% pass rate and reduced release cycle time.

frameworks.title: Dependencies, Blockers & Enablers
frameworks.summary: Key dependencies across QA/SDET roles include Clear Requirements, Stable Test Environment, Dev Readiness, Test Data Availability, and Stable Builds, each with a named risk if unmet. Mitigations include freezing requirements before sprint start, coordinating with DevOps for environment uptime, close coordination with dev to stabilize APIs/UI, and evaluating tools early; enabling support comes from the Product Owner, PM, Senior SDET, and QA Director.

frameworks.title: Expected Artifacts
frameworks.summary: QA artifacts: Test Plans & Test Cases, Test Execution Reports, QA Sign Off, Defect Logs, Traceability Matrix, Test Summary Reports. SDET artifacts: Automation Framework Documentation, Automated Test Suites, CI/CD Execution Reports, Defect Reports with Root Cause Analysis, Automation Coverage Reports.

roles.title: Senior UX/UI Designer
roles.mission: To lead and deliver high-quality, user-centered digital experiences by applying advanced UX research, design strategy, and visual execution skills, while mentoring junior designers and collaborating with stakeholders to align design outcomes with business goals.
responsibilities: Apply and evolve research methods to evaluate user needs and share insights.
Plan and facilitate workshops and usability tests independently.
Translate research and workflows into journey maps, prototypes, and polished UI aligned with design systems.
Mentor junior designers and contribute to design knowledge-sharing across the organization.
Most important activities: research execution, prototyping, visual design delivery, mentoring, stakeholder alignment.
Non-essential activities: direct business strategy ownership (led by Head/Director level).
Dependencies: product managers, dev teams, stakeholder input.
Blockers: lack of user access, unclear business goals.
Enablers: strong design systems, research access, clear product vision.
30 days: audit current projects and design systems, begin leading usability testing.
60 days: plan and run a workshop, create detailed prototypes with annotations.
90 days: deliver a full design cycle (research → flows → prototypes → UI) and present outcomes to stakeholders.

behavioral: Mentorship and coaching of junior designers

metricsAndKras.outcomeArea: Apply and evolve user research methods
metricsAndKras.metric: Number of research activities independently conducted. Depth and clarity of research analysis reports.
metricsAndKras.target: Deliver 3+ independent research reports by Year 6. Positive stakeholder feedback on research insights influencing product decisions.

metricsAndKras.metric: Number of workshops facilitated. Number of usability tests executed independently. Quality of synthesized outputs (reviewed by stakeholders).
metricsAndKras.target: Successfully lead at least 2 workshops by Year 6. 2+ usability test findings directly incorporated into product design.

metricsAndKras.outcomeArea: Deliver high-quality user flows, prototypes, and UI
metricsAndKras.metric: Number of flows/prototypes delivered. Contributions to design system evolution. Timeliness and quality ratings from design leads.
metricsAndKras.target: Deliver 3+ annotated prototypes within sprint cycles by Year 6. At least 2 new design system components proposed and approved.

metricsAndKras.outcomeArea: Mentor junior designers and contribute to thought leadership
metricsAndKras.metric: Number of mentorship sessions or buddy assignments completed. Knowledge-sharing contributions (show & tells, team docs).
metricsAndKras.target: At least 2 junior designers mentored successfully by Year 6. Minimum 2 knowledge-sharing sessions conducted.

roles.title: Lead UX/UI Designer
roles.mission: To lead design strategy, drive user-centered innovation, and ensure the delivery of exceptional user experiences by connecting research insights with design execution, mentoring team members, and aligning stakeholders across business, design, and technology.
responsibilities: Translate user research into actionable insights, reports, and design strategies.
Plan, facilitate, and synthesize workshops to drive collaboration and decision-making.
Define usability test strategies, analyze results, and guide product improvements.
Lead design reviews, establish design standards, and ensure accessibility and inclusion.
Mentor designers, manage stakeholder expectations, and contribute to the design community.
Most important activities: leading research synthesis, usability test strategies, design reviews, stakeholder alignment.
Non-essential activities: routine pixel-level design (delegated to mid-level designers).
Dependencies: cross-functional teams, user access, product leadership.
Blockers: lack of clear product vision, limited user access.
Enablers: research repositories, analytics tools, mature design system, leadership buy-in.
30 days: audit design systems, review ongoing projects, start leading usability strategies.
60 days: facilitate workshops, synthesize outputs into actionable priorities.
90 days: deliver end-to-end design cycle with research synthesis, flows, prototypes, and stakeholder presentations.

behavioral: Coaching and career development for team members

metricsAndKras.outcomeArea: Drive user research synthesis and organizational standards
metricsAndKras.metric: Number of research reports/presentations delivered. Evidence of contribution to organizational research practices.
metricsAndKras.target: 3+ actionable research reports delivered annually. At least 1 organizational method/standard contributed by Year 8.

metricsAndKras.outcomeArea: Deliver advanced design execution and strategy
metricsAndKras.metric: Number of workshops facilitated. Number of usability tests executed independently. Quality of synthesized outputs (reviewed by stakeholders).
metricsAndKras.target: Successfully lead at least 2 workshops by Year 6. 2+ usability test findings directly incorporated into product design.

metricsAndKras.outcomeArea: Deliver high-quality user flows, prototypes, and UI
metricsAndKras.metric: Number of optimized flows and journeys delivered. Timeliness and quality of sprint deliverables. Peer and stakeholder review scores on design quality.
metricsAndKras.target: Deliver end-to-end journeys for 2+ projects annually. Maintain 90%+ on-time delivery across sprints.

metricsAndKras.outcomeArea: Mentor designers and manage stakeholder alignment
metricsAndKras.metric: Number of mentees supported. Career progression outcomes (measured via performance reviews). Stakeholder satisfaction scores.
metricsAndKras.target: Successfully mentor at least 2 junior designers per year. Positive stakeholder alignment feedback in 80%+ of initiatives.

frameworks.title: Design Roles OKRs with Targets
frameworks.summary: Defines quarterly-style OKRs (Objective / Key Results / Metrics / Source Data / Success Indicator-Target) for the Associate, UX/UI, and Sr. UX/UI Designer levels only — it does not include a Lead UX/UI Designer section. Covers research-session participation, on-time task delivery, idea-sharing, and note-sharing turnaround. It closes with a separate, level-unspecified department table setting targets for deliverable review approval (>=95%), periodic usability reviews (>=2/quarter), design rework rate (<8%), design-critique/coaching cadence (>=2 sessions/month), mentee assignment coverage (100% of juniors), stakeholder satisfaction (>=80%), and on-time annotated handoffs (>=95%).

frameworks.title: Design Roles OKRs with Metrics & Source Data
frameworks.summary: Provides the most complete per-level breakdown, covering all four design role levels (Associate, UX/UI, Sr. UX/UI, and Lead UX/UI Designer). Each level has 4-5 Objectives, each paired with Key Results, Metrics, Source Data, and a Success Indicator/Target, spanning UX research growth, prototype/design delivery quality, communication and storytelling, and (from Sr. UX/UI upward) mentoring and stakeholder/thought-leadership outcomes. This is the authoritative source used for each role's metricsAndOkrs above.
frameworks.source: Design Roles OKRs with Metrics & Source Data.docx

accountabilities: Maintain complete documentation and stakeholder alignment

Stakeholder Collaboration – Work with business, operations or any other role to refine requirements.
Process Flows, Story Maps – Create supporting documentation.
Design discussions – Work with the design team to get the designs and get the sign-off from the stakeholders.
Participate in sprint ceremonies (e.g., standups, retros) and clarify story details for developers.
Support UATs Functional Testing – Assist in validation before release.
Help with Data Analysis – Help with the data analysis, if needed, for decision making.

frameworks.title: Business Analyst OKR Framework
frameworks.summary: Defines BA OKRs across three weighted objectives: delivering high-quality requirements with minimal rework (UAT query rate ≤ 10% of stories per sprint via JIRA logs, weight 20%; Requirement Defect Leakage Rate ≤ 10% via JIRA bug root-cause tagging, weight 20%), improving collaboration and sprint effectiveness (dev flags reduced to <10% per sprint, weight 20%; 90% sprint stories signed off before the upcoming 2 sprints, weight 20%), and maintaining documentation/stakeholder alignment (100% of meetings documented with MoM and communicated via email, weight 20%).

frameworks.title: Senior Business Analyst OKR Framework
frameworks.summary: Defines Sr. BA OKRs across three weighted objectives: aligning the product backlog with strategic business goals (90%+ of backlog items tagged to business OKRs in JIRA, weight 30%; 90% sprint stories signed off before upcoming 2 sprints, weight 20%), delivering post-release value through metrics improvement (75% of releases show ≥5% improvement in key product metrics such as NPS or drop-offs, weight 25%), and supporting team development and process maturity (mentor 2+ BAs per quarter with documented feedback sessions, weight 10%; 'R%' of roadmap milestones delivered on time and within scope, weight 15% — weight/value appears to contain a typo in the source document).

frameworks.title: Product Manager OKR Framework
frameworks.summary: Defines PM OKRs across three weighted objectives: driving product strategy and measurable outcomes (≥75% of PM's own OKRs met per quarter tracked in Keka, weight 30%; Stakeholder Confidence Index ≥4.0/5.0 via quarterly survey, weight 20%), prioritizing high-impact features based on data (75% of backlog stories scored using RICE/ICE, weight 20%; 2 data-led prioritization conflicts documented/resolved per month, weight 10%), and mentoring BAs to grow team capability (2+ BAs mentored into high-ownership roles annually, weight 10%; 360° feedback average ≥4.2 from mentored team, weight 10%).

frameworks.title: Senior Product Manager OKR Framework
frameworks.summary: Defines Sr. PM OKRs across three weighted objectives: making strategic go/no-go product investment decisions (90% of product proposals evaluated with a documented ROI model, weight 25%; 80% of funded initiatives meet their adoption/revenue goal within 1–2 quarters, weight 20%), building scalable product team capabilities (100% of PMs have documented OKRs aligned to org vision, weight 20%; 3+ frameworks or playbooks launched, weight 15%), and ensuring roadmap discipline and execution quality (≥85% of roadmap items delivered per quarter, weight 10%; Stakeholder Confidence Index ≥4.2 surveyed quarterly, weight 10%).

frameworks.title: Revised KPIs/OKRs (Sr. PM)
frameworks.summary: A separate, later 'Revised KPIs/OKRs' table that explicitly names the Sr. PM/SPM role with its own weighted objectives: driving product strategy (≥75% of own OKRs met per quarter, weight 10%; Stakeholder Confidence Index ≥4.0/5.0, weight 20%), prioritizing high-impact features (75% of backlog scored via RICE/ICE, weight 10%), mentoring BAs/Sr. BAs/PMs and growing team capability (5+ mentored into high-ownership roles annually, weight 20%; initiatives launched and accepted by the SPM's reporting manager, weight 10%; a 6+ month rolling roadmap existing for every project the SPM is aligned to, weight 10%; the Sr. PM helping management decide whether to proceed with product decisions, weight 20%). The doc notes this implies 100% of PMs/Sr. BAs/BAs have documented OKRs aligned to org vision, since the KPI tables for each role already cover this.

roles.mission: Own end-to-end delivery outcomes for assigned client accounts or programs, ensuring predictable delivery, healthy margins, strong client relationships, and high-performing teams.
accountabilities: Team performance, engagement, and capacity readiness
Compliance with delivery governance and quality standards
responsibilities: Delivery Ownership
Own end-to-end delivery across assigned projects/programs.
Ensure adherence to scope, timelines, quality, and SLAs.
Actively manage risks, dependencies, and trade-offs across teams.
Financial Ownership
Own project/program budgets, revenue realization, and margins.
Track billing milestones, change requests, and commercial closures.
Optimize utilization and cost efficiency without compromising delivery.
Client & Stakeholder Ownership
Own client confidence and satisfaction for assigned accounts.
Act as primary escalation point for delivery issues.
Drive regular governance reviews, steering committees, and status forums.
People & Capacity Ownership
Lead and develop Project Managers, Tech Leads, and delivery teams.
Own hiring, onboarding, and ramp-up readiness in partnership with ER/TA.
Drive engagement, retention, and performance management.
Governance & Improvement Ownership
Enforce delivery governance, metrics, and reporting discipline.
Identify and implement process improvements and automation.

behavioral: Owns It: Takes full accountability for delivery, financial, and client outcomes; never attributes failure to "the team".
Empathy: Balances client pressure with team sustainability; manages trade-offs with emotional intelligence.
Professional Maturity: Handles difficult client conversations, escalations, and negotiations calmly and credibly.
Collaboration: Works seamlessly across Sales, PMs, Engineering, Finance, and HR.
technical: Delivery & Execution Discipline: Strong command over Agile/Hybrid delivery, RAID management, and governance cadence.
Financial Acumen: Manages budgets, margins, billing milestones, and change requests with commercial rigor.
Problem Solving & System Thinking: Anticipates delivery risks and resolves systemic issues, not just symptoms.
Stakeholder Management: Maintains executive-level client confidence through clarity and predictability.

frameworks.title: Contributor–Owner–Leader (COL) Framework
frameworks.summary: Provides the common language across Taazaa for career development, performance evaluation, and organizational design. The delivery org is organized around outcome ownership rather than activity management: Contributors execute with excellence, Owners ensure outcomes are delivered, and Leaders multiply impact by building systems and developing other leaders.

frameworks.title: Galbraith's Star Model Application
frameworks.summary: Applies Jay Galbraith's Star Model (Strategy, Structure, Processes, Rewards, People) to Taazaa's delivery function: delivery as a profit center where every delivery leader owns P&L; a matrix of vertical (account) ownership by Delivery Managers and horizontal (program) orchestration by Program Managers; standardized governance with AI-enabled risk scanning and status automation; KPI-weighted performance scorecards; and a 4-stage career architecture.

frameworks.title: RACI Accountability Framework
frameworks.summary: Resolves role overlap, particularly between the Delivery Manager and Program Manager, by mapping activities to a single Accountable owner across seven domains: Strategy & Planning, Delivery Execution & Oversight, Financial Management, Risk Management, Client & Stakeholder Management, People/Team/Capacity, and Governance/Process/Continuous Improvement, plus an Artifacts Ownership table.

frameworks.title: Career Architecture: The 4-Stage Growth Journey
frameworks.summary: Defines delivery career progression across four stages — Contributor, Owner, Portfolio Leader, and Executive — each with a distinct focus and key metric, from Project Coordinator/Associate Project Manager through Project Manager/Technical PM/Senior Project Manager, to Program Manager/Delivery Manager/Director of Delivery, up to Chief Delivery Officer, including critical transition points (Contributor→Owner, Owner→Leader) and common pitfalls at each transition.

frameworks.title: Governance & Operating Model
frameworks.summary: Defines the delivery governance cadence (forum, frequency, owner, participants, and purpose from Sprint Ceremonies through Quarterly Business Review), a four-level escalation ladder from PM up to CDO/CEO, and a decision rights matrix specifying who decides and who is consulted for common delivery scenarios (e.g., extending client SOW, resource allocation, re-prioritization across programs).

frameworks.title: Performance & KPI Architecture
frameworks.summary: Sets out weighted KPI scorecards for the Director of Delivery (Portfolio Health, Process Compliance, Financial Health), Delivery Manager (on-time delivery, account margin, billing realization, CSAT, attrition), and Project Manager (Portfolio Profitability, Billing Realization, Attrition Rate, Backfill Turnaround, Appraisal Effectiveness, On-Time Delivery, Leadership Score) roles, each with specific targets.
